message.content:
This is a very strong candidate. The commit `c593863a8` fixes an out-of-bounds read in the regex parser when parsing word boundary assertions. The bug is: when the regex ends with a backslash `\`, the parser reads `*current_` which is past the end of the string. This is a stack-buffer-overflow READ.

The test case is `new RegExp("                                \\")` - a regex with a trailing backslash. The READ 2 suggests reading 2 bytes (a UTF-16 char16_t).

Let me verify this is the right fix. The issue is a stack-buffer-overflow READ 2. The regex parser reads `*current_` which is a `char16_t` (2 bytes). When the regex ends with `\`, `current_` points past the end of the buffer, and reading `*current_` reads 2 bytes out of bounds.

Let me check the current state of the code in the vulnerable version (HEAD) to confirm the bug exists.
